AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structures in Animal production? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structures in Animal production.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structures in Animal production.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structures in Animal production.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Structures in Animal production.

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Production Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Production Structures.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Production Structures.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Production Structures.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Production Structures.

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agroforestry? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agroforestry.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agroforestry.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agroforestry.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Agroforestry.

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Aquaculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Aquaculture.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Aquaculture.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Aquaculture.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Parasite control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Parasite control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Parasite control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Parasite control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Parasite control.

13. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Pest control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Pest control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Pest control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Pest control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Pest control.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Rearing Selected Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Rearing Selected Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Rearing Selected Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Rearing Selected Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Rearing Selected Animals.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Digestive systems of animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Digestive systems of animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Digestive systems of animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Digestive systems of animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Digestive systems of animals.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Vegetative propagation? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Vegetative propagation.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Vegetative propagation.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Vegetative propagation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Vegetative propagation.

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water conservation.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Products.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Products.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Products.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Products.

20. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

21. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Inorganic fertilisers? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Inorganic fertilisers.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Inorganic fertilisers.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Inorganic fertilisers.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Inorganic fertilisers.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Powered Tools and Equipment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Management of Agro- byproducts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Agri- business Accounts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Inorganic fertilisers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Water conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Vegetative propagation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Agroforestry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Protection: Pest control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

31. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Production Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

32. In three clear sentences, explain Digestive systems of animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
